questions.question: Which of the following policy adoptions by the Government of India is NOT guided by the 'Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Preparation of building by-laws**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy** are guidelines to the central and state governments of India, to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• Promotion of village panchayats is guided by the Directive Principles, aiming at decentralization of power and democratic governance at the grassroots level.
 
• Uniform civil code is mentioned under Article 44 of the Directive Principles, promoting a uniform legal framework for all citizens irrespective of religion.
 
• Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor is guided by Article 47, aiming at improving public health and nutrition levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• These are a set of guidelines or principles given to the governing body of a country for establishing a just society.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning their implementation cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution of India from Article 36 to Article 51.
 
• They aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of village panchayats**
 
 
• This is mentioned under Article 40 of the Directive Principles.
 
• It aims at organizing village panchayats and endowing them with the necessary powers and authority to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)**
 
 
• Article 44 of the Constitution of India directs the state to secure a Uniform Civil Code for the citizens throughout the territory of India.
 
• The goal is to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set governing every citizen.
 
 
 
• **Prohibition of consumption of alcoholic liquor**
 
 
• Article 47 of the Directive Principles emphasizes the state's duty to improve public health by prohibiting the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs.
 
• The idea is to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.
 
 
 
• **Building By-laws**
 
 
• Building by-laws are a set of standards and regulations set by the local government to control and regulate the construction of buildings.
 
• They ensure that constructions are safe, healthy, and in accordance with the urban planning norms.
 
• They typically include regulations on building height, floor area ratio, setbacks, and other construction norms.
 
• Building by-laws are not specifically mentioned in the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.question: What is the exterior angle of a regular 15-sided polygon?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of sides of the polygon (n) = 15

**Formula Used:**

Exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360º / n

**Calculation:**

Exterior angle = 360º / 15

⇒ Exterior angle = 24º

**The exterior angle of a regular 15-sided polygon is 24º.**

questions.question: In which soil does cotton grow best?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black soil**__.

__
 
• Black soil is also known as **Regur soil** and is ideal for growing cotton.
 
• It is **rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime**, which are essential nutrients for cotton growth.
 
• Black soil has a high moisture-retaining capacity, making it suitable for cotton farming.
 
• This soil is predominantly found in the **Deccan Plateau** region, covering parts of Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Brown soil is a type of **loam soil** that is typically fertile and suitable for growing various crops.
 
• It is well-draining and rich in organic matter but not particularly suitable for cotton cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**
 
 
• Red soil is rich in **iron oxide** which gives it a reddish color.
 
• It is commonly found in parts of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh but is less suitable for cotton due to its lower nutrient content and poor moisture retention.
 
 
 
• **Yellow Soil**
 
 
• Yellow soil is formed by the weathering of ancient crystalline rocks and is found in parts of Orissa and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is less fertile compared to black soil and not ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.question: An air jet covers a certain distance at a speed of 144 km/h in 5 hours. To cover the same distance in 2 hours, what is the required speed of the air jet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the air jet = 144 km/h

Time taken = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Required Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Distance = 144 km/h × 5 hours

Distance = 720 km

Required Speed = 720 km / 2 hours

⇒ Required Speed = 360 km/h

**The correct answer is option 1 (360 km/h).**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arthropod**__.

• **Arthropods** are a phylum of invertebrate animals having an exoskeleton, a segmented body, and jointed appendages.
 
• The phylum Arthropoda includes insects, arachnids, myriapods, and crustaceans.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs, which enable them to have greater mobility and adaptability in various environments.
 
• They are the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, encompassing more than 80% of all described species.

• This phylum includes marine animals like starfish, sea urchins, and sand dollars.
 
• Echinoderms have a unique water vascular system used for locomotion and feeding.
 
• They exhibit radial symmetry as adults, which is different from the bilateral symmetry seen in arthropods.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Annelida**
 
 
• Annelids include segmented worms like earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes.
 
• They have a segmented body but lack jointed appendages.
 
• Annelids have a coelom, a fluid-filled body cavity that provides a hydrostatic skeleton.
 
 
 
• **Phylum Nematoda**
 
 
• Nematodes, or roundworms, are unsegmented worms with a cylindrical body.
 
• They have a complete digestive system but lack jointed appendages.
 
• Many nematodes are parasitic, affecting plants, animals, and humans.

questions.question: The L.C.M. of (2)/(3), (3)/(4), (4)/(5), (9)/(11) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Fractions: 2/3, 3/4, 4/5, 9/11

**Formula Used:**

L.C.M. of fractions = L.C.M. of numerators / H.C.F. of denominators

**Calculation:**

Numerators: 2, 3, 4, 9

Denominators: 3, 4, 5, 11

Step 1: Find L.C.M. of numerators:

L.C.M. of 2, 3, 4, 9

Prime factorization:

2 = 2¹

3 = 3¹

4 = 2²

9 = 3²

L.C.M. = 2² × 3² = 4 × 9 = 36

Step 2: Find H.C.F. of denominators:

H.C.F. of 3, 4, 5, 11

3 = 3¹

4 = 2²

5 = 5¹

11 = 11¹

Since there are no common prime factors, H.C.F. = 1

Step 3: Calculate L.C.M. of fractions:

L.C.M. = L.C.M. of numerators / H.C.F. of denominators

⇒ L.C.M. = 36 / 1

⇒ L.C.M. = 36

**The L.C.M. of 2/3, 3/4, 4/5, 9/11 is 36.**

questions.question: Article 43 B in Part Ⅳ of the Constitution of India deals with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooperative societies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 43B in Part IV of the Constitution of India explicitly deals with the **promotion of cooperative societies**.
 
• It mandates the state to promote **voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management** of cooperative societies.
 
• This article falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable but aim to guide the state in formulating policies and laws.
 
• The inclusion of Article 43B was brought about by the **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**, highlighting the importance of cooperatives in the Indian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in citation while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court for their violation.
 
• The main aim of DPSPs is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**
 
 
• This amendment added a new Part IXB to the Constitution, which is dedicated to cooperative societies.
 
• It aims to encourage economic activities of cooperatives which in turn help progress rural India.
 
• It also made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c).
 
• This amendment also inserted Article 43B in the DPSPs to ensure the promotion of cooperatives.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies in India**
 
 
• Cooperative societies are voluntary associations of individuals having common needs who combine forces for the achievement of common economic interests.
 
• They play a significant role in the socioeconomic development of the country, especially in rural areas.
 
• Examples include agricultural cooperatives, consumer cooperatives, housing cooperatives, and many more.
 
• The Indian government has been actively promoting cooperative societies through various schemes and legislative measures to enhance their functioning and management.

questions.question: Manipuri classical dance form often depicts scenes from the life of God _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Manipuri classical dance, also known as Jagoi, is one of the major Indian classical dance forms originating from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• This dance form often depicts scenes from the life and the divine play (Ras Lila) of Lord Krishna, who is a major deity in Hinduism.
 
• Manipuri dance is characterized by graceful and fluid movements and is deeply religious and spiritual in nature.
 
• The dance form encompasses both solo and group performances, with the Ras Lila being a popular group performance that narrates the love story of Krishna and Radha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri Dance:**

 
 
• Manipuri dance is one of the eight classical dances of India and is particularly known for its themes based on the Vaishnavism tradition of Hinduism, which emphasizes the worship of Lord Vishnu and his avatars, especially Krishna and Rama.
 
• Vaishnavism is one of the major traditions within Hinduism that reveres Vishnu and his avatars as the supreme deities.
 
• The Ras Lila, a major theme in Manipuri dance, is a dramatic enactment of the love story between Krishna and Radha, and it is performed during special occasions and festivals, especially on the night of the full moon.
 
• The dance form includes various genres such as classical, folk, and tribal forms, with each genre showcasing unique aspects of Manipuri culture and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Lord Krishna:**
 
 
• Lord Krishna is one of the most widely revered and popular Hindu deities, known for his role in the Mahabharata and the Bhagavad Gita.
 
• He is considered the eighth avatar of Vishnu and is often depicted as a divine lover, cowherd, and supreme being.
 
• Krishna's life and teachings are a central theme in many Hindu texts, including the Bhagavad Gita, the Bhagavata Purana, and various other scriptures and folklore.
 
• His divine play, or Leela, especially his youthful escapades with the gopis (milkmaids) of Vrindavan, is a significant theme in various Indian classical dance forms, including Manipuri.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• India has a rich tradition of classical dance, with eight officially recognized classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi, and Sattriya.
 
• Each dance form has its own distinctive style, techniques, costumes, and themes, often rooted in ancient Indian texts and traditions.
 
• These classical dances are not just forms of entertainment but are also deeply connected to religious and spiritual practices in India.
 
• They often involve intricate footwork, expressive hand gestures (mudras), and facial expressions, with performances narrating mythological stories, religious themes, and cultural traditions.

questions.question: A train covers a distance of 12 km in 25 minutes. If its speed is decreased by 5 km/hr, then the time (in minutes) taken by it to cover the same distance will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered by the train = 12 km.

Time taken = 25 minutes = 25/60 hours = 5/12 hours.

Initial speed = Distance / Time

Speed = 12 / (5/12) = 12 × 12 / 5 = 144 / 5 = 28.8 km/hr.

**Formula Used:**

New time taken = Distance / New speed

**Calculation:**

New speed = Initial speed - Decrease in speed

New speed = 28.8 km/hr - 5 km/hr = 23.8 km/hr

New time taken = Distance / New speed

New time taken = 12 km / 23.8 km/hr

New time taken in hours = 12 / 23.8

New time taken in hours = (12)/(23.8)

New time taken in hours = (6)/(11.9)

New time taken in minutes = (6)/(11.9) × 60

New time taken = 3600/119 = 30(30)/(119)

**The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: With which substance does silver react and turn black?

• This reaction is known as tarnishing, which commonly affects silverware and jewelry.
 
• The formation of silver sulphide is a chemical change where silver (Ag) reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H2S) or other sulphur compounds.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a task in 12 days. B and C together can finish it in 18 days. If A is three times more efficient than C, then in what time B alone would finish the same task?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can finish a task in 12 days.

B and C together can finish it in 18 days.

A is three times more efficient than C.

**Formula Used:**

Work formula: 1 day's work of A + 1 day's work of B = 1/12

Work formula: 1 day's work of B + 1 day's work of C = 1/18

Efficiency relation: A = 3C

**Calculation:**

Let the efficiency of C be C units/day.

Then the efficiency of A = 3C units/day.

Let the efficiency of B be B units/day.

From the first work formula:

1 day's work of A + 1 day's work of B = 1/12

⇒ 3C + B = 1/12

From the second work formula:

1 day's work of B + 1 day's work of C = 1/18

⇒ B + C = 1/18

Solving the two equations:

Equation 1: 3C + B = 1/12

Equation 2: B + C = 1/18

Subtracting Equation 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ (3C + B) - (B + C) = 1/12 - 1/18

⇒ 2C = 1/12 - 1/18

⇒ 2C = (3 - 2) / 36

⇒ 2C = 1 / 36

⇒ C = 1 / 72

Substitute C back into Equation 2:

⇒ B + 1/72 = 1/18

⇒ B = 1/18 - 1/72

⇒ B = (4 - 1) / 72

⇒ B = 3 / 72

⇒ B = 1 / 24

So, B alone can finish the task in 24 days.

**The correct answer is option 1.**

• **The Single European Act, 1986:**
 
 
• Signed on 17 February 1986 and came into force on 1 July 1987.

• Laid the groundwork for the subsequent Maastricht Treaty.
 
 
 
• **The Treaty of Amsterdam, 1997:**

• Focused on reforms to enhance the efficiency of the EU, including more power to the European Parliament and changes in immigration and asylum policies.

What is the value of the following expression:

**Given:**

Expression: (1 + x) (1 + x²) (1 + x⁴) (1 + x⁸) (1 - x)

**Calculation:**

First, pair (1 + x) and (1 - x)

Next, multiply the result with (1 + x²)

⇒ (1 - x²)(1 + x²) = 1 - x⁴

Now, multiply this result with (1 + x⁴)

⇒ (1 - x⁴)(1 + x⁴) = 1 - x⁸

Finally, multiply with (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 - x⁸)(1 + x⁸) = 1 - x¹⁶

**The value of the expression is (1 - x¹⁶).**

questions.question: If the selling price is doubled, the profit becomes three times the original. Find the new profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If the selling price is doubled, the profit becomes three times the original.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) = 100 (assume for simplicity)

Let the original Selling Price (SP) = SP

Original Profit = SP - CP

Original Profit Percentage = ((SP - CP) / CP) × 100

When SP is doubled, New SP = 2 × SP

New Profit = 2 × SP - CP

Given that New Profit = 3 × Original Profit

⇒ 2 × SP - CP = 3 × (SP - CP)

⇒ 2 × SP - 100 = 3 × (SP - 100)

⇒ 2 × SP - 100 = 3 × SP - 300

⇒ 2 × SP - 3 × SP = -300 + 100

⇒ -SP = -200

⇒ SP = 200

Original Profit = SP - CP = 200 - 100 = 100

Original Profit Percentage = (100 / 100) × 100 = 100%

New Profit = 3 × 100 = 300

New Profit Percentage = (300 / 100) × 100 = 300%

**The new profit percentage is 300%.**

questions.question: Who is called the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Minto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Minto is referred to as the 'Father of Communal Electorate' in India because of his role in the introduction of separate electorates.
 
• During his tenure as Viceroy of India, the Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, was enacted.
 
• The Morley-Minto Reforms allowed for separate electorates for Muslims, which meant that Muslims could elect their representatives separately.
 
• This was a significant step in the constitutional history of India as it institutionalized communal representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act of 1909**

 
 
• Also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, named after the Secretary of State for India, John Morley, and the Viceroy of India, Lord Minto.
 
• It introduced a limited increase in the involvement of Indians in the governance of British India.
 
• The act allowed for the inclusion of elected Indian members in the legislative councils, both at the central and provincial levels.
 
• The most notable feature was the introduction of separate electorates for Muslims, which meant that Muslims could elect their representatives separately from the Hindus.
 
• This move was aimed at addressing the demands of the Muslim community and ensuring their political representation.
 
 
 
• **Communal Electorate**
 
 
• It refers to the system of separate electorates in which voters of a particular community vote for their representatives separately.
 
• This system was introduced to provide political representation to minority communities.
 
• While it aimed to ensure fair representation, it also led to the division of society along communal lines.
 
• The system was later criticized for fostering communalism and was eventually abolished after India gained independence.
 
 
 
• **Lord Minto**
 
 
• He served as the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910.
 
• His tenure is particularly noted for the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
 
• These reforms were part of the British strategy to address the growing demands for Indian participation in governance.
 
• Lord Minto is often criticized for introducing separate electorates, which many believe laid the foundation for communal divisions in Indian politics.

Distance Covered = Number of Revolutions × Circumference of the Wheel

Circumference of the Wheel = 2πr

where r is the radius of the wheel

Distance Covered = 1000 × 2πr

154,000 = 1000 × 2 × (22/7) × r

**The radius of the wheel is 24.5 meters.**

questions.question: Six bells commence tolling together and toll at the intervals of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 seconds respectively. In the first 10 minutes, how many times would they have tolled together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Intervals at which the six bells toll: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 seconds

Time period: 10 minutes = 600 seconds

**Formula used:**

To find how many times the bells toll together, we need to calculate the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the intervals (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12).

The number of times they toll together in the given period is calculated by dividing the total time by the LCM.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12:

Prime factorization of 2 = 2

Prime factorization of 4 = 2²

Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

Prime factorization of 8 = 2³

Prime factorization of 10 = 2 × 5

Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

The LCM is the highest powers of all primes:

LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 = 120 seconds

Step 2: Calculate the number of times they toll together in 600 seconds:

After 1st time the total number of times bells toll together = 600/120

Including the 1st time the total Number of tolls = dfrac{600}{120} + 1 = 5 + 1 = 6

**Conclusion:**

The bells will toll together 6 times in the first 10 minutes.

Profit ratio to Cost Price = Profit / Cost Price

• The original Constitution of India did not contain Fundamental Duties.
 
• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were 10 Fundamental Duties enumerated in Article 51A of the Constitution.

• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• They are included in Part IV-A of the Constitution.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, but they are essential for the overall development of the country.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• Known as the "Mini Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact.
 
• Introduced significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002:**
 
 
• Made education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years under Article 21A.
 
• Added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A (k) which states that a parent or guardian must provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• Set up by the Government of India in 1976 to recommend changes to the Constitution.
 
• Its recommendations led to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.

questions.question: India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SLV–3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3) was the first satellite launch vehicle developed by India.
 
• SLV-3 was developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) under the guidance of Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
 
• The first successful launch of SLV-3 took place on July 18, 1980, which placed the Rohini satellite into orbit, making India the sixth country to have satellite launch capabilities.
 
• The development of SLV-3 was a significant milestone in India's space program, marking the beginning of indigenous satellite launch capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASLV (Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle)**

 
 
• ASLV was designed to augment payload capacity compared to SLV-3.
 
• It was used to place satellites into low Earth orbit (LEO).
 
• ASLV had a mixed record of success and was eventually phased out in favor of more advanced launch vehicles.
 
 
 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• GSLV is designed to launch heavier payloads into geostationary orbits.
 
• It uses a cryogenic upper stage, which enhances its payload capacity.
 
• GSLV is crucial for launching communication satellites.
 
 
 
• **PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle)**
 
 
• PSLV is known for its reliability and versatility.
 
• It is used to launch satellites into polar orbits and geostationary transfer orbits.
 
• PSLV has been instrumental in launching numerous Indian and foreign satellites.

questions.question: Chandrayaan–1, India's first spacecraft mission to the moon, was successfully launched by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PSLV–C11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **PSLV–C11** is a version of India's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV).
 
• Chandrayaan–1, India's first lunar probe, was launched successfully by PSLV–C11 on **22 October 2008**.
 
• PSLV–C11 was developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• This mission marked India's entry into lunar exploration and demonstrated its capability to launch and manage complex missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle)**

 
 
• GSLV is another type of launch vehicle developed by ISRO designed to launch heavier payloads into geostationary orbits.
 
• It is used primarily for deploying communication satellites.
 
 
 
• **GSLV Mk III**
 
 
• GSLV Mk III, also known as LVM3, is the heaviest and most powerful rocket developed by ISRO.
 
• It is capable of carrying large payloads and was used for the Chandrayaan–2 mission.
 
 
 
• **RLV–TD (Reusable Launch Vehicle-Technology Demonstrator)**
 
 
• RLV–TD is an experimental project by ISRO to develop technologies for a reusable space launch vehicle.
 
• The aim is to reduce the cost of access to space.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan–1**
 
 
• Chandrayaan–1 was India's first mission to the moon and aimed at high-resolution remote sensing of the lunar surface.
 
• The mission was instrumental in confirming the presence of water/hydroxyl on the moon.
